subject: Post-demo technical recap — auth, routing & response contract
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo technical recap — auth, routing & response contract

Alyssa, thanks again for taking the demo today — great questions from the platform team. Quick recap and a few specific technical clarifications we need to finalize the integration plan so our engineers can start a short trial. Summary + ask below.

TL;DR: Redwood can support API-key and OAuth flows; we recommend chat (streaming) for multi-turn assistants and completions for single-shot transforms. Need confirmation on your desired auth mode, model routing preferences, and whether you want an embeddings->reranker two-step pipeline or a single-step reranker.

What we covered (attachments):
- Attached: lightweight integration checklist (redwood_integration_checklist_v1.pdf) and a mutual action plan (switchgrid-mutual-action-plan.xlsx).

Questions for SwitchGrid (please reply inline):
1) Auth: do you want us to provision API keys managed by Redwood, or integrate your OAuth/SSO (you mentioned Okta)? If OAuth, do you have a service account flow we can use for the test environment?
2) Routing & fallbacks: you mentioned wanting low-cost fallbacks during load. Which policy do you prefer? (a) latency-first (always prefer faster Llama-3-small style variants), (b) cost-first (fallback to quantized CPU variants), or (c) region-aware (route to closest region then fallback).
3) Response contract: will you accept function/tool-calling structured JSON for deterministic post-processing, or do you need free-text completions and downstream parsers? If structured, do you want strict schema validation on Redwood's side?
4) Embeddings & reranker: do you want us to compute embeddings client-side and call a reranker model, or use a single-model reranker? For high-precision retrieval, we usually recommend embeddings + a cheap reranker.
5) Tokenization & limits: do you need explicit guarantees on max_tokens per response or stop-token behavior for censoring? We want to align on counting (input+output) and on whether you prefer response truncation or request rejection when limits exceed.
6) Streaming: do you expect character-by-character partial deltas (server push) or chunked sentence-level streaming? This matters for SDK examples.

Next steps (proposed):
- You reply to the questions above by EOD Wed (12/16).
- Laura will draft an SDK/auth snippet for your SREs once auth mode is confirmed.
- We'll land a 2-week trial config in your tenant and run a 1k-query smoke test with production prompts.

Thanks — I looped in Laura and Karthik for technical answers below.

—

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side to unblock Laura/Karthik: 

1) Auth: we want to use our Okta SSO; service-account OAuth flow is preferred for machine-to-machine. We can provide client credentials for a test service account.
2) Routing: latency-first sounds best for customer-facing flows; fallback to cost-first for batch backend jobs. We can define two policies keyed by route.
3) Response contract: we'd strongly prefer structured JSON via tool-calling for response fields our UI consumes (title, summary, action_items). For generative summary fields we can accept free text. No need for Redwood-side strict validation initially; we can run validation client-side.
4) Embeddings/reranker: embeddings + lightweight reranker is our preference to keep reranker compute bounded.
5) Tokenization & limits: we need predictable truncation semantics. Prefer deterministic rejection over silent truncation for the first phase (fail fast). We'll want explicit token accounting in logs.
6) Streaming: chunked sentence-level streaming is fine; we don't need character deltas. Prefer to receive events at sentence boundaries so our UI can render coherent lines.

I'll attach a short internal doc with our SRE contact and Okta client id in a follow-up. Happy to jump on a quick sync tomorrow morning if helpful.

Alyssa — awesome, thanks for the rapid replies. Below are implementation notes and recommended snippets so your SREs know what to expect. I included concrete guidance for SDK setup, routing, structured output, embeddings/reranker, and tokenization semantics.

AUTH (OAuth service-account)
- Redwood supports client-credential OAuth for private tenants. We'll exchange an OAuth client-id/secret and return short-lived bearer tokens for SDK use.
- For dev/test we can also support API-keys if you prefer to start faster; prod we recommend OAuth tied to Okta.
- Action: please share the test client_id and redirect URIs for secure validation.

SDK / HANDOFF SNIPPET (pseudo):
- SDK init: authenticate with bearer token returned from our token endpoint. Example header: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Token rotation: SDK will auto-refresh using the client credentials flow; we can provide a sample refresh handler.

ROUTING & FALLBACKS
- We support route-level policies. Implementation options:
  * route=customer_ui -> latency-first -> prefer gpu-small models, fallback to region-compatible small variants.
  * route=batch_pipeline -> cost-first -> send to quantized CPU pool or lower-precision variants.
- We can expose these as simple strings in the request metadata: {"route": "customer_ui"}.

STRUCTURED OUTPUT / TOOL CALLING
- For deterministic fields (title, summary, intent, action_items) use a function calling contract. Example: model returns {"tool":"structured_summary","args":{...}}.
- If you want Redwood to enforce schema, we can run a lightweight JSON schema validator in the runtime and return 400 with a schema-mismatch error. You indicated you will handle validation client-side initially — that's fine.

EMBEDDINGS + RERANKER
- Recommended: compute dense embeddings for candidates, do retrieval, then call a small reranker model with (query_embedding, candidate_texts) to produce a score and final ordering.
- Cost/latency: embeddings are fairly cheap; reranker is model-size dependent. We'll provision a 2-3x throughput headroom for smoke tests.

TOKENIZATION, max_tokens, STOP BEHAVIOR
- Token accounting: Redwood reports tokens as input_tokens + output_tokens. max_tokens param applies only to the model output; if input + max_tokens exceed model context, the request is rejected (if you choose fail-fast) or truncated (if you choose best-effort). You asked for fail-fast — we'll configure the request to return a 413-like error with a token-exceeded code.
- stop tokens: we support both token-based stop sequences (model-side) and application-level post-processing. For structured output we recommend model-side stop to avoid partial JSON.

STREAMING SEMANTICS
- We can offer chunked sentence-level streaming. Implementation: the runtime will emit events at punctuation boundaries when available; SDK receives an ordered stream of "delta" objects. We'll provide an option to buffer until sentence breaks if your UI prefers whole-sentence updates.

NEXT STEPS / TECH Handoff
- Ben: we'll need the Okta test client_id and SRE contact.
- Alyssa / SG: confirm route names for customer_ui and batch_pipeline (we can adopt your existing route tags).
- Action items owner: Laura (build SDK snippet), Karthik (provision trial dev tenant), SwitchGrid SRE (supply credentials).

I'll attach the SDK snippet and a minimal JSON schema example in the Drive link Ben shared. If helpful, we can spin up a 30-min tech pairing with your SREs tomorrow afternoon.
